finding.claim: When the caller passes subject=X to decode()/decode_complete() and the token has no 'sub' claim, _validate_sub returns early and the subject is never compared. Sibling checks for aud and iss raise MissingRequiredClaimError in the same situation, so this check fails open. Severity low to medium, status PLAUSIBLE: RFC 7519 makes sub optional, so this may be intentional.
finding.source: Token string and the subject= argument to decode()/decode_complete() (jwt/api_jwt.py:305-318, 378). Precondition: attacker holds a validly signed token from the same issuer that omits 'sub' (for example a service or client-credentials token).

trace.note: decode_complete passes subject into _validate_claims after signature verification
_validate_sub returns early when 'sub' is absent, before the comparison
The subject comparison that is skipped for sub-less tokens
Sibling aud check raises MissingRequiredClaimError when aud is missing but audience was supplied
Sibling iss check raises MissingRequiredClaimError when iss is missing but issuer was supplied

finding.guards_checked: Signature is verified first (jwt/api_jws.py:269-277), so the token must come from a trusted key. verify_sub defaults to True (jwt/api_jwt.py:60). The sub type check runs only when sub is present (jwt/api_jwt.py:449-450). No other code path in the package enforces the subject when sub is absent.
